ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure gives four candidate control circuits, labeled A, B, C, and D respectively. Each circuit contains button contacts, labeled SB1, SB2, as well as contactor coil KM; some circuits also draw a lower parallel auxiliary branch. Figure C is located in the lower left corner. In the main loop, SB2, SB1, and the KM coil on the right can be seen connected in series. There is also a parallel branch below, but the contacts of this branch are labeled KM1 and KM2, not the correct auxiliary contact structure directly used for self-locking holding of this KM coil. Reasoning: The phenomenon required by the question is: when the start button SB2 is pressed, contactor KM can pull in; but after SB2 is released, KM immediately releases. This indicates that the circuit can temporarily form a path when SB2 is pressed, but there is no effective self-locking holding loop. Analyzing Figure C, after SB2 is pressed, current can reach the KM coil through SB2 and SB1, so KM can be energized and pull in; when SB2 is released, the SB2 contact opens again, and the lower parallel branch in Figure C is not the correct self-locking contact that plays a holding role for the same KM coil, so it cannot continue to supply power to the KM coil, and KM immediately loses power and releases. Therefore, the one that conforms to this phenomenon is Figure C.

raw_record.question_text: Which circuit diagram shows this phenomenon: after pressing the start button SB2, the contactor KM is energized, but as soon as SB2 is released, the contactor KM immediately de-energizes?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: there are four candidate control circuits A, B, C, and D, each containing push buttons labeled SB1/SB2 and a contactor coil labeled KM, with some candidates showing an auxiliary branch. Use the question text to set the required behavior: KM energizes while SB2 is pressed, but drops out immediately when SB2 is released. Then trace graph C: with SB2 pressed, the series path through SB2 and SB1 reaches the KM coil, so KM can energize. After SB2 is released, SB2 reopens; because the parallel lower branch in C is not a proper KM self-locking auxiliary contact for the same coil, it cannot maintain current. Therefore KM de-energizes immediately, so the matching diagram is graph C.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中给出了四个候选控制电路，分别标为 A、B、C、D。每个电路都包含按钮触点，标注有 SB1、SB2，以及接触器线圈 KM；部分电路还画有下方的并联辅助支路。C 图位于左下角，主回路上可以看到 SB2、SB1 与右侧 KM 线圈串联，下方还有一条并联支路，但该支路的触点标注为 KM1、KM2，不是直接用于该 KM 线圈自锁保持的正确辅助触点结构。
推理：题目要求的现象是：按下启动按钮 SB2 时，接触器 KM 能吸合；但松开 SB2 后，KM 立即释放。这说明电路在 SB2 被按下时能临时形成通路，但没有有效的自锁保持回路。按 C 图分析，按下 SB2 后，电流可经 SB2、SB1 到达 KM 线圈，因此 KM 能得电吸合；当松开 SB2 后，SB2 触点重新断开，而 C 图下方的并联支路不是对同一 KM 线圈起保持作用的正确自锁触点，所以无法继续给 KM 线圈供电，KM 立即失电释放。因此符合该现象的是 C 图。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses direct state-by-state current-path tracing combined with the seal-in/holding-contact rule; this is the natural single robust route for this circuit-identification problem.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the four labeled circuit diagrams A–D. Identify in each the positions of SB2, SB1, the KM coil, and any lower parallel/self-holding branch. In graph C, note that pressing SB2 can complete the top series path to the KM coil, but the lower branch is not a valid self-holding path for the shown KM coil because its contacts are labeled separately as KM1/KM2 rather than the same KM auxiliary contact.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the wording to identify the target phenomenon: temporary energization on pressing SB2 and immediate loss of energization when SB2 is released.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: A contactor remains energized after a momentary start button is released only if a normally open auxiliary contact of the same contactor KM is wired in parallel with the start button to form a seal-in circuit. If the start button opens and no valid KM-controlled holding contact bypasses it, the coil immediately loses power.
